I don't think I will have time to have a look at what happens soon but that's definitely likely to happen :)

issue.title: Cannot switch back and forth between an external with new_local_repository and new_http_repository

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
I've run into a problem where bazel seems to get confused when switching between an external configured using "new_local_repository" and "new_http_repository".  

Brief context:  I'm developing on Ubuntu trusty, and am using some system installed packages in a C++ application.

In my particular instance, I started with boost configured as a new_local_repository to use the system installed boost.  At some later point, I decided to use a newer version of boost as a new_http_repository.  That all worked fine.  However, after that, if I use git to switch back and forth between the two states, bazel gets confused and is unable to build the new_http_repository version if it has already built it once, and then built the new_local_repository version since.

I have a minimal test repository on github which demonstrates this problem for me.

```
git clone https://github.com/jpieper-tri/bazel_local_http_external.git
cd bazel_local_http_external
git checkout master^
bazel build //...  # this is the first build on new_local and works fine
git checkout master
bazel build //... # this is the first build with new_http and works fine
git checkout master^
bazel build //... # this also works fine
git checkout master
bazel build //... # fails
```

The failure I see looks like:

```
$ bazel build //...
INFO: Found 1 target...
ERROR: missing input file '@boost//:boost_1_61_0/libs/python/src/exec.cpp'.
ERROR: /home/jpieper/.cache/bazel/_bazel_jpieper/49d5c2f61756db305af8ff7531250266/external/boost/BUILD:87:1: @boost//:boost_python: missing input file '@boost//:boost_1_61_0/libs/python/src/exec.cpp'.
Target //src:sample failed to build
Use --verbose_failures to see the command lines of failed build steps.
ERROR: /home/jpieper/.cache/bazel/_bazel_jpieper/49d5c2f61756db305af8ff7531250266/external/boost/BUILD:87:1 1 input file(s) do not exist.
INFO: Elapsed time: 3.724s, Critical Path: 0.02s
```

And the version of bazel tested with:

```
bazel version
Build label: 0.2.3
Build target: bazel-out/local-fastbuild/bin/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/BazelServer_deploy.jar
Build time: Tue May 17 14:21:13 2016 (1463494873)
Build timestamp: 1463494873
Build timestamp as int: 1463494873
```

issue.title: bazel server crashes with internal error if @ accidentally included in repository name

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

bazel completely crashes when creating a repository with a name accidentally prefixed with `@`, such as with a typo like `name = "@rules_pkg"`.

```
$ bazel build
Starting local Bazel server and connecting to it...
[...]
Internal error thrown during build. Printing stack trace: java.lang.RuntimeException: Unrecoverable error while evaluating node '[/homeworld/test]/[WORKSPACE], 1' (requested by nodes 'EXTERNAL_PACKAGE:[/homeworld/test]/[WORKSPACE]')
[...]
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: com.google.devtools.build.lib.cmdline.LabelSyntaxException: invalid repository name '@@rules_pkg': workspace names may contain only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-', '_' and '.'
[...]
```

For obvious reasons, this should not be expected to work -- but I would expect a nice error, rather than an `Internal error thrown during build.` report and an immediate crash of the bazel server. It would also be nice for the bazel server to keep running in the presence of this error.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

This WORKSPACE suffices:

```
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:git.bzl", "git_repository")

git_repository(
    name = "@rules_pkg",
    commit = "b1014c8e56c27cc8199eaf747e671d0c32582175",
    importpath = "github.com/bazelbuild/rules_pkg",
)
```

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

I'm using a Debian Buster chroot.

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

```
$ bazel info release
release 2.1.0
```

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

I've found https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/374 and https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/977, but they're not that relevant.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?
